cards.question: What does the presentation-builder fork add on top of the upstream script-to-HTML deck factory?
cards.answer: A grounded-deck pipeline: EVERY number on a slide carries a claim id traced back to verified evidence.
cards.explanation: Worked case: the three-scenario CRM deck under `projects/crm-three-scenarios/`. The method is packaged as the skill `structured-citation-metagraph`. Upstream only turns a script plus a style reference into one HTML file.
cards.anchor: Every number on the slide wears a luggage tag; pull its string and you land on the shelf, the page and the sentence it came from.
cards.evidence_quote: the deck is rendered from the graph with the claim id on every number; two scripts refuse to pass anything that is not grounded

cards.question: Which invariant does presentation-builder's `structured-citation-metagraph` skill exist to protect?
cards.answer: The presentation-layer rule: everything shown traces to evidence, and NOTHING shown is a recommendation.
cards.explanation: The CRM deck shows grounded truth against three scenarios and offers no choice. Breaks if undone: the deck becomes a pitch that a sceptical reader can dismiss. The fields that make a fact traceable: see 10.
cards.anchor: A guide unlocks three rooms and describes each one to the centimetre, then stays silent when asked which room to rent.
cards.confusables: decision layer — it RECOMMENDS one option; the presentation layer only shows grounded truth against all of them.
cards.evidence_quote: Its one invariant is the presentation-layer rule: nothing is shown that cannot be traced to a source, a locator and a quote, and nothing shown is a recommendation.

cards.question: presentation-builder: complete the rule `grounded_ok()` applies before a view may cite a node.
cards.cloze: An `evidence_fact` is grounded when one evidence entry holds {{c1::source}}, {{c1::locator}} AND {{c1::quote}}; any other node needs a {{c2::grounded_in}} edge path to such a fact.
cards.explanation: The path is followed transitively and is cycle-safe; an id missing from the graph is not grounded. Breaks if undone: a story or metaphor node with no measurement behind it reaches a slide as if it were a fact.
cards.confusables: the workflow script's `EVIDENCE` schema — it requires ONLY `source` and `locator`; the guard also demands `quote` (see 91).
cards.evidence_quote: res = any(ev.get("source") and ev.get("locator") and ev.get("quote") for ev in evs)

cards.question: presentation-builder: a claim verdict (`confirmed`, `caveat`, `refuted`) vs a health-check verdict (`keep`, `simplify`, `consolidate`, `pay_for`): what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: A claim verdict says whether a FACT survived verification; a health-check verdict says what to do with a built ITEM, and is never given to a scenario.
cards.explanation: Claim verdicts come from the two verifier lenses and decide the wording a slide may carry. Health-check verdicts come from the rank agent and become `health_verdict` edges in the graph.
cards.anchor: A proofreader stamps a sentence true, hedged or false; next door a mechanic hangs a keep-or-scrap label on a machine. Neither stamp fits the other's object.
cards.confusables: health-check verdict (`keep | simplify | consolidate | pay_for`) — it rates a built ITEM; a claim verdict rates the EVIDENCE of one fact.
cards.evidence_quote: Verdicts are about items, never about scenarios.

cards.question: presentation-builder · `structured-citation-metagraph` procedure: recite the 7 steps from the boundary brief to the commit.
steps: orchestrator writes `projects/<name>/brief.md` -> request, tagged sources, conventions
explorers, one per source family in parallel -> items, facts and gaps with evidence
rank agent -> `implementation-health-check.md` and `cost-lines.md`, one verdict per item
metagraph agent -> `metagraph.json`, planned views, ledger; `citation_graph.py` must pass
verifiers, two lenses per batch -> confirmed, caveat or refuted; maintainer applies them
presentation agent renders from the graph -> each number carries `data-claim`
QA loop, hygiene, commit -> render, fact drift, design rules, `deck_cites_check.py`
cards.answer: brief · explore · rank · metagraph · verify · present · QA + hygiene + commit
cards.explanation: Each role writes its full output to the project folder and returns a typed summary, so the orchestrator reads summaries and paths, never the raw material. Verify sits BEFORE present on purpose (see 60).
cards.anchor: A trial day: the judge rules what is admissible, clerks gather exhibits, an appraiser grades them, a wall map links them, two cross-examiners attack, then the advocate speaks and an usher checks.
cards.evidence_quote: → metagraph (hierarchy, edges, planned views, ledger, guard script) → verify (two lenses per batch; confirm, caveat, refute; side-findings filed) → present

cards.question: presentation-builder · verdict merge in `workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js`: predict the `status` the code below assigns to the claim described in its first line.
cards.answer: `caveat` — ANY `refuted` verdict wins, else any `caveat`, else `confirmed`; a claim that received no verdict at all becomes `unverified`.
cards.explanation: (1) No verdict is `refuted`, so `refuted` is false. (2) One verdict is `caveat`, so `caveat` is true. (3) The ternary chain returns 'caveat'. The stricter lens always wins; only non-confirmed results are sent to the maintainer agent.
cards.confusables: `unverified` — given when NO lens returned a verdict for the claim; `confirmed` needs at least one verdict and none worse.

cards.question: Which command in presentation-builder regenerates `metagraph.md` and enforces the grounded-path guard?
cards.explanation: `scripts/` is the skill's own folder; a near-identical copy (one line differs: the node-type order in `render_md`) also sits in `projects/crm-three-scenarios/`. It scores co-cited pairs, REPLACES the Markdown file (never appends) and exits 2 when a view cites an ungrounded node (see 90).
cards.example: python3 scripts/citation_graph.py --graph metagraph.json --dry-run  # prints each node's top neighbours, writes nothing, the guard still runs
cards.anchor: A doorman at the slide-room door: each guest shows an unbroken chain of receipts back to a quoted source, or the whole queue is sent home.
cards.confusables: `--dry-run` — prints the neighbours and WRITES no file; the guard runs in both modes.

cards.question: presentation-builder · `citation_graph.py --dry-run`: predict the `combined`, `co` and `prox` values printed for the pair described below.
cards.answer: `combined=1.550 co=2 prox=0.500` — proximity is 1 / 2 ** (4 - 3) = 0.5 for a parent and its child, and 0.7 * 2 + 0.3 * 0.5 = 1.55.
cards.explanation: (1) A child shares its parent's whole chain: shared ancestor depth 3. (2) prox = 1 / 2 ** (4 - 3) = 0.5. (3) combined = 0.7 * 2 + 0.3 * 0.5 = 1.55, printed with three decimals. Proximity halves per unshared level, so it only breaks ties between equally co-cited nodes.
cards.confusables: co-citation — COUNTS the views that cite both nodes (weight 0.7); folder proximity only reads the parent chain (weight 0.3).
cards.evidence_quote: | 2 | 0.500 | 1.550 | same branch, two shared slides: the fact that *defines* the problem |

cards.question: Which script in presentation-builder checks the claim ids the BUILT deck shows against the metagraph?
cards.answer: `deck_cites_check.py` in the skill's `scripts/`: unknown, non-fact or refuted ids exit 1.
cards.explanation: It reads `data-claim="Cxxx"` from HTML, or `^Cxxx^` / `[Cxxx]` from Markdown, and lists every caveated claim so the caveat wording can be confirmed on the slide. `--strict` also fails on ids that no view planned.
cards.example: python3 scripts/deck_cites_check.py --graph metagraph.json --deck deck.html --strict  # exit 1 on unknown, refuted or unplanned ids
cards.confusables: `citation_graph.py` — guards the PLAN (what each view intends to cite); this script guards the BUILD (what the deck actually shows).
cards.evidence_quote: This script closes the other gap: what the *built deck* actually shows.

cards.question: Which file in presentation-builder's `projects/crm-three-scenarios/` is the single context boundary every agent reads first?
cards.answer: `brief.md`: the request verbatim, the admissible sources with provenance tags, the output conventions.
cards.explanation: The user's stories and tables are admissible as what was asked, never as truth. Breaks if undone: agents cite material nobody declared admissible. Write it INSIDE the repository: locators that point at a scratch directory die with the session.
cards.anchor: A chalk circle drawn on the floor before anyone enters: each worker steps into it first, and nothing lying outside it may be picked up.
cards.evidence_quote: This file is the ONLY context boundary.

cards.question: How does presentation-builder's workflow script fan out the verification of the claims?
cards.answer: It slices the claims into batches of `BATCH = 8` and runs EVERY batch under two lenses, source fidelity and numeric-and-logical consistency, inside one `parallel(...)` call.
cards.explanation: Worked case: 20 batches x 2 lenses = 40 verifiers. Two DIFFERENT lenses find different errors; identical refuters would not. A barrier follows: verdicts are merged per claim before anything is edited (see 21).
cards.confusables: QA loop — also parallel, but it checks the finished DECK (render, fact drift, design rules); the verify fan-out attacks CLAIMS before any slide exists.

cards.question: Why does presentation-builder's skill verify every claim BEFORE the presentation agent writes the deck rather than fact-check the finished deck?
cards.answer: The deck is then written with the caveated wording already decided, so QA has ONLY layout to fix; verifying afterwards turns every refutation into a slide rewrite.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: a refuted number already sits on a slide and in the spoken script, and each one costs a rewrite. Worked case: QA round 1 found five blocking issues, all layout, nothing factual.
cards.anchor: A sign painter letters prices on the shop window before the inspector arrives; every wrong price is then scraped off the glass by hand.
cards.confusables: fact-drift QA — it runs once the deck exists and only checks that slides still match the verified claims; it does NOT re-open the sources.
cards.evidence_quote: Verifying after writing makes every refutation a slide rewrite.

cards.question: Why does presentation-builder's `build_pptx.py --pptx` pass `--reference-doc reference.pptx` to pandoc rather than rely on pandoc's stock template?
cards.answer: The stock template sets body text at 24 pt, which overflows the denser slides; `reference.pptx` is pandoc's own template with body text at 16 pt and titles at 26 pt.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: text runs past PowerPoint's content placeholder, because `chunk()` budgets `LINES_PLAIN = 11` lines per slide for 16 pt text.
cards.anchor: A removal list counted in small boxes: load the same list packed in big boxes and the last ones stick out of the van door.
cards.confusables: `--budget` — changes how many LINES go on one slide; `reference.pptx` changes the font SIZE those lines are estimated for.
cards.evidence_quote: pandoc's stock template sets body text at 24 pt, so expect overflow on the denser slides

cards.question: presentation-builder: what does `citation_graph.py` print when a metagraph is safe to render, and how does a failed guard show?
cards.answer: It prints `guard OK: every cited node in N views is grounded`. A failure prints `PRESENTATION-LAYER GUARD FAILED` with the offending views on stderr and exits 2.
cards.explanation: Before a commit the skill also wants `metagraph.md` byte-identical on a second run. Once the deck exists, `deck_cites_check.py` is the matching check on the build (see 32).
cards.example: python3 citation_graph.py --graph metagraph.json --out metagraph.md; echo $?  # 0 after the guard OK line, 2 after GUARD FAILED
cards.evidence_quote: print(f"guard OK: every cited node in {len(views)} views is grounded")

cards.question: presentation-builder: you reuse the skill's bundled `references/workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js` unchanged on a second project. Which of the skill's own rules does that script break, and what is the smallest fix for each?
cards.answer: It still carries first-run behaviour: reuse its phase shape, rewrite its prompts. (1) Its `EVIDENCE` schema requires ONLY `source` and `locator`, so a fact with no quote passes the tool layer and fails the guard once a view cites it: add `quote` to `required`. (2) Its maintainer prompt REMOVES refuted claims, while the skill keeps the node with `status: refuted`: rewrite that rule. (3) `VERDICT_SCHEMA` has no `side_findings`, so verifiers cannot file what they meet: add the field.
cards.explanation: The script also never calls `deck_cites_check.py`; the skill lists it as a QA step. The guard itself is already strict: `grounded_ok()` demands all three evidence fields (see 10).
